title: A Kingdom That Will Not Heal
overview: God describes Israel's northern kingdom as full of lies, palace plots and desperate foreign deals, and grieves that it never turns back to him.

parts.label: Healing blocked (vv. 1-2)
parts.note: God speaks like a doctor who keeps trying to heal Israel, but every attempt uncovers more lying, burglary and robbery. Ephraim and Samaria are names for the northern kingdom and its capital, and the people act as if God neither sees nor remembers.

parts.label: Plots around the throne (vv. 3-7)
parts.note: The royal court enjoys the people's crimes and flattery, and at a royal celebration the officials drink heavily with the king while scheming. Like an oven that smolders all night and flares at dawn, their plotting waits and then erupts, which probably reflects the string of murdered kings in Israel's last decades.

parts.label: A half-baked loaf (vv. 8-10)
parts.note: Israel has blended into the surrounding nations and is like flatbread on hot stones that was never flipped, burnt on one side and raw on the other. Foreign powers drain its strength and its decline shows like graying hair, yet it does not notice or turn back to the LORD.

parts.label: A dove flying both ways (vv. 11-12)
parts.note: Caught between two empires, Israel's kings kept switching between asking Egypt and asking Assyria for help. God says he will catch them in a net like a bird hunter, and the kingdom did fall to Assyria around 722 BC after its last king turned to Egypt.

parts.label: Cries that miss God (vv. 13-14)
parts.note: God says he longs to rescue them, but they tell lies about him and only wail in distress instead of truly calling to him. Cutting themselves was a ritual for pleading with other gods for good harvests, though the Hebrew word is uncertain and some translations say instead that they assemble for grain and wine.

parts.label: A bow that misses (vv. 15-16)
parts.note: God trained and strengthened them, yet they turn against him and are like a faulty bow that never hits its target. Their leaders will fall, and Egypt, the very power they trusted, will mock them.

think: What makes slow decline so hard to notice in ourselves or our communities, like gray hair that appears without our seeing it?
